newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas sees another slow day, only two trades.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas sees another slow day, only two trades.

text.p: The IPE natural gas futures market saw another disappointing day on Wednesday, with only 50 lots traded in two separate deals - although even this was an improvement on the previous day, with only 20 lots done.

A futures broker said that there were still bids and offers being posted across most periods, and that although the volumes done were "not pleasing", it was an indication of a wide market rather than one on which dealers have given up.
He stressed that despite several days of minimal volumes, there was no suggestion that the market was failing, and added that the OTC market has also been quiet.
The two deals transacted were both done in February, with the last trade done at 17.355 pence a therm, up by 0.180 pence a therm from Tuesday's settlement price.
Bids and offers were wide apart on most other months, and no bids were posted at all on four of the 12 monthly contracts.
By 1550 GMT, a total of 130 lots of Exchanges for Physical had been transacted.
